title: Dr. Krishan Kumar Named AAPI President-Elect, Outlines Vision for Global Expansion
excerpt: The veteran physician and educator, who will become AAPI president in July 2027, plans to strengthen membership, expand international partnerships, and mentor next-generation Indian-American doctors.
body:
• Dr. Krishan Kumar assumed the role of President-Elect of the American Association of Physicians of Indian Origin (AAPI) on July 1, 2026, and will become President in July 2027.
  • Kumar, a Clinical Professor at NYIT College of Osteopathic Medicine, has served AAPI for over 25 years across multiple leadership roles, including Treasurer and Vice President.
  • His agenda prioritizes strengthening AAPI membership benefits, expanding global outreach, mentoring second-generation physicians, and building international healthcare partnerships.
  • AAPI represents over 120,000 physicians of Indian origin, who treat roughly one in every seven patients in the United States.

Kumar Steps Into President-Elect Role at Tampa Convention

Dr. Krishan Kumar, a veteran physician, educator, and emergency medicine specialist, officially assumed the role of President-Elect of the American Association of Physicians of Indian Origin (AAPI) on July 1, 2026, during a ceremony at AAPI headquarters in Oak Brook, Illinois. He takes the position alongside Dr. Meher Medavaram, who became AAPI President for the 2026-27 term, according to reports in the Malayalam Daily News and India Post.

Kumar will serve as President-Elect through the current term before ascending to the presidency in July 2027, when he will lead the largest ethnic medical organization in the United States. AAPI represents over 120,000 physicians of Indian origin and is considered the second-largest medical association in the country after the American Medical Association.

"This victory belongs to all of us. It is a testament to the power of unity, collaboration, and the belief that together, we can achieve great things. Let us move forward together, with determination and hope, to build a brighter future for our community."

— Dr. Krishan Kumar, AAPI President-Elect

A Career Spanning Five Decades in Medicine and Education

Kumar currently serves as Clinical Professor of Pediatrics and Emergency Medicine at the New York Institute of Technology College of Osteopathic Medicine (NYITCOM), where he has been on faculty since 2011. Previously, he chaired the Department of Pediatrics and directed the residency program at Nassau University Medical Center in New York, where he expanded clinical care and training programs serving underserved communities.

"Let us move forward together, with determination and hope, to build a brighter future for our community."</p><cite>— Dr."

As Medical Director of the Nassau County Fire Police EMS Academy, Kumar has trained more than 5,000 Emergency Medical Technicians and over 300 paramedics, strengthening emergency response capacity at both regional and national levels. He also sits on the New York State Board of Medicine and holds fellowships with the American College of Emergency Physicians, the American Academy of Pediatrics, and the American College of Sports Medicine.

In June 2026, NYIT conferred upon Kumar the prestigious Doctor of Science (Honoris Causa) degree at its convocation ceremony, attended by more than 7,000 graduates and guests. The institution recognized his "enduring dedication to medical education and public service," placing him among fewer than 200 physicians in the United States known to hold both MD and Doctor of Science degrees, according to India Post.

Plans to Strengthen AAPI From Within

Kumar's elevation to President-Elect caps a 25-year trajectory within AAPI. He served as Treasurer in 2021-22, was elected Vice President for the 2025-26 term—becoming the first member from AAPI's Queens and Long Island chapter to hold a national office in nearly three decades—and now moves into the President-Elect position alongside a new executive team that includes Dr. Sreeni Gangasani as Vice Chair, Dr. Soumya Neravatla as Secretary, and Dr. Raghu Lolabhattu as Treasurer.

His agenda centers on several core priorities: strengthening the value and benefits of AAPI membership, increasing organizational transparency and accountability, empowering state chapters and specialty societies, and promoting physician wellness and professional development. Speaking at the AAPI Global Healthcare Summit in Bhubaneswar, Odisha, in January 2026, Kumar signaled his preference for actionable programs over abstract aspirations.

"These discussions are not just academic—they are actionable. Our goal is to bring evidence-based solutions to the forefront of India's healthcare landscape."

— Dr. Krishan Kumar, at the AAPI Global Healthcare Summit 2026

Expanding AAPI's Global Footprint

Kumar takes the leadership reins at a moment of significant international expansion for AAPI. At the organization's 44th Annual Convention in Tampa, Florida, in early July 2026, Nita Ambani announced the India-America Health Alliance, a landmark partnership between the Reliance Foundation and AAPI. The alliance commits to providing telemedicine consultations to patients in rural India via Jio's 5G network, training first responders in advanced clinical protocols and artificial intelligence, and producing up to 500 peer-reviewed publications over the next decade, according to Business Wire.

Internationally, Kumar has played a pivotal role in advancing Emergency Medicine, EMS, and Disaster Medicine training programs in India, contributing to the formal recognition of these specialties in the country. He has championed expanded residency slots, legal aid for AAPI members, and stronger ties with global medical associations such as the Global Association of Physicians of Indian Origin (GAPIO), which represents 1.4 million Indian-origin doctors worldwide.

AAPI has also launched a nationwide Stem Cell Donor Drive in partnership with cricket legend Sunil Gavaskar and the DATRI Blood Stem Cell Donors Registry. Kumar highlighted the urgency of expanding the donor pool during the campaign. "70% of patients lack a family match. For Indians, the odds are even lower due to the limited donor pool," he said, according to India Post.

What It Means for the Indian-American Medical Community

Indian-origin physicians make up approximately 10 percent of all doctors in the United States and nearly 50 percent of International Medical Graduates practicing in the country. They care for roughly one in every seven patients nationally. For this community, Kumar's presidency—expected to begin in July 2027—represents a continuation of AAPI's push toward greater visibility, advocacy, and cross-border healthcare collaboration.

Kumar's immediate priorities include engaging second-generation Indian-American physicians, a growing demographic within AAPI, and expanding mentorship programs for medical students and residents from India seeking U.S. residency placements. AAPI operates more than 130 local chapters across the country and runs CME programs, health fairs, and charitable projects in both the United States and India.

With the India-America Health Alliance now announced and the Global Healthcare Summit series continuing, Kumar will have substantial institutional momentum behind him when he takes the presidential gavel next year. His path from the Queens and Long Island chapter to the top of a 120,000-member organization underscores AAPI's tradition of recognizing leaders who, as Kumar put it, believe that "medicine is ultimately about service."
